cells.tense: You are holding the weight in front of you without hardening around it right now.
cells.ask: Name one weight that is yours to carry, say it out loud, and keep carrying it without telling anyone it is heavy.
cells.core:
You're carrying something right now without making it a performance. Not gritting through it and not pretending it isn't there — the weight is real and you're still moving, still in touch with what's around you. That's the hard version of strength, the one that stays soft.
There's a direction in this too. Something you actually want is what all this effort is for, and you can feel it even when you don't name it. That recognition is doing quiet work. What you're bearing today is being borne toward something, and you can tell what that something is without a lot of argument. Let that be enough for now.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding it without going hard.
cells.verb: bearing what must be borne while holding form
cells.place: the pull toward what you actually want

cells.tense: You will be braced against a weight that has not arrived yet, and will keep bracing.
cells.ask: Take one thing you are guarding against and put it down on a real surface — a desk, a table — for one hour today.
cells.core:
You're ahead of everything, muscles tight, waiting for the hit that hasn't come. Somewhere ahead is a picture where the weight lands and you're ready for it — so you're ready for it now, and now, and now. The preparing has become the whole day.
The strength is real. That's the trouble. It's just gripping something that isn't here, and the grip is eating the very thing the strength was for. There's a want under all the bracing, and you can't see it while your eyes are fixed on the far edge. Set something down and let the surface hold it. You don't have to hand it to anyone.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing for weight that hasn't landed.

cells.tense: You were at a door that opened once, and you are still standing on the old side of it.
cells.ask: Say one true thing you want to someone who has no power over whether you get it, and then let the conversation end wherever it ends.
cells.core:
Something got dropped. You were going to bear it, and then you didn't, and after that the bearing felt like too much to ask of yourself. So you stopped asking anything of yourself, and the thing you were aimed at went dim behind you.
The strength isn't gone, it's just not being spent. You're not weak — you are careful, and the care has gone past the point of protecting anything. Putting more effort into that spot won't bring it back. Let something be finished so there's room again. A want you've been sitting on can be said out loud without needing the answer to be yes.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped asking anything of yourself, and the aim went dim.

cells.tense: You are already carrying it and moving toward a want you keep saying you don't have.
cells.ask: Pick one task you've been calling someone else's job and say, in one sentence, that it's yours — then do the next small part of it today.
cells.core:
Look at what you've been doing this week. You've held things together that didn't want to be held, and you've moved toward something you wanted, and you keep describing both as if they happened on their own. The strength is running. The want is live. You just haven't signed either one.
That's not modesty, exactly. It's more that you've been looking past yourself the whole time, waiting for the real version of this to show up. There's a smaller, earlier form of the same thing under your feet — something you wanted before it got complicated — and it still points where you're already walking. You can say that out loud without it becoming a boast.
cells.sheetLine: You're already carrying it and you keep saying you aren't.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim in the draft is that the person has already recognized the star they steer by, when the record only says Inspiration is orientation, not that it has arrived. A reader could reasonably say they have no star yet, or that the star keeps changing, and the reading may read as pressure to name one prematurely. The asks survive a wrong read because each is a small physical act — taking one step, holding something whole, saying a thing as wanted — that gives information about the person either way. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line where the card's strength gets praised as a trait rather than described as work the person is already doing.
